claims.text: In July 2013, NASA's Cassini slipped into Saturn's shadow.
That blue dot is Earth, 1.44 billion kilometres away.
1.44 bn km the farthest group photo you might be in

On 19 July 2013, NASA's Cassini slipped into Saturn's shadow, so the Sun was hidden behind the planet and the rings lit up from behind. Then it looked back. Under the rings, 1.44 billion km away, is a tiny blue dot: Earth, with the Moon a faint bump beside it. It was the first time people on Earth knew in advance that their picture would be taken from that far away.

Sources:
NASA, The Day the Earth Smiled (PIA17172): https://images.nasa.gov/details/PIA17172
NASA, The Day the Earth Smiled: Sneak Preview (PIA17171): https://images.nasa.gov/details/PIA17171

Images: NASA / JPL-Caltech / Space Science Institute (Cassini). Narration uses a synthetic voice.

review.notes: From NASA captions PIA17172/PIA17171: 19 July 2013, Cassini in Saturn's shadow with the Sun eclipsed (no damaging glare), rings backlit; Earth a blue dot 898 million miles (1.44 bn km) away, the Moon a faint protrusion; the first time inhabitants knew in advance; people joined social events to celebrate (the event name is 'The Day the Earth Smiled'). The marker sits on the blue dot at (0.728, 0.526) of PIA17171, checked on the image. The card label 'the farthest group photo you might be in' is a framing line, not a measured claim.
